comparisons.evidence: P's Transition Gateway makes meditation "the doorway to a habit that already exists," directly inheriting daily frequency. Q's Sponsor-a-Session argues that "one employer partnership can move thousands of users," but distribution and sponsorship do not as directly ensure that those users become daily active users.

P explains that a gateway "inherits frequency from an existing daily behaviour" and that the Causality Lab creates repeated demand for another measurement. Q's Commons Stewardship expects a dipping "collective calm" score to raise individual sessions, while Sponsor-a-Session assumes awareness of third-party payment will improve adherence; both require less-supported motivational leaps.

P anticipates concrete failure modes such as gateway "bypass rates," measurement fatigue, and departure-related abandonment. Q's leading mechanisms require enterprise sales and privacy-sensitive aggregate reporting for Sponsor-a-Session, while Commons Stewardship proposes a "semi-synthetic" collective score that risks distrust or perceived manipulation.

P specifies a "browser extension that intercepts the first calendar-meeting link," a 45-second protocol, a control condition, and kill criteria. Q also offers tests, but concepts such as "Frictionless Delivery" merge the contradictory pathways of making meditation an app-opening toll and eliminating the app open through SMS or voice.

P combines unusual but plausible levers such as meditation as a personal causal experiment, fixed "departures," emotional reconciliation, and a session that changes device state. Q introduces distinctive financial and communal ideas, but several novel-looking proposals reduce to table-stakes gamification or reminders, including the "Near-Miss Progress Bar," "Meditation Exchange Market," and state-triggered notification.

P credibly spans behavioural gateways, self-measurement, scarcity and synchrony, functional state changes, physical triggers, and therapist integration. Q similarly spans third-party financial stakes, passive co-presence, environmental objects, teaching-to-learn, collective stewardship, and concealed content; neither has a clear breadth advantage after weak variants are discounted.

P converges on three mechanisms with distinct causal roles and explicitly rejects weaker overlaps such as "transit aesthetics rather than transit mechanics." Q elevates the speculative Sponsor-a-Session and Commons Stewardship while retaining diluted or ineligible additions such as Un-App delivery, state-triggered notifications, and the rejected Near-Miss mechanism.
